entries.appliesTo: residential rental property owners (and their agents, representatives, or subcontractors) and owners of rent-pricing coordinators — software, data analytics services, or entities performing a coordinating function — plus coordinator agents/representatives/subcontractors

exposure.enforcer: New Jersey Antitrust Act enforcement (cross-referenced; includes civil actions per § 5)

sources.prohibition: § 3 — 'It shall be unlawful and a violation of the "New Jersey Antitrust Act," P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-1 et seq.) for: a. a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, … to subscribe to, contract with, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of services of a coordinator; b. the owner of a coordinator to facilitate an agreement among rental property owners that restricts competition with respect to residential dwelling units, including by performing a coordinating function; … c. two or more rental property owners to engage in consciously parallel pricing coordination … d. any agent or representative of a coordinator or subcontractor thereof to engage in consciously parallel pricing coordination'
sources.enforcer: § 4 — 'Sections 7 through 17 of the "New Jersey Antitrust Act," P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-7 through 56:9-17) shall apply for a violation pursuant to section 3 of this act.'

flags: Text on file is the First Reprint (doc_id 3390099, Amended 2026-03-10); later versions (Comm Sub 2026-06-09, Amended 2026-06-24) extracted to 0 chars per manifest — final enacted text may differ from what was coded
Enforcement is a pure cross-reference to NJ Antitrust Act §§ 7-17 (§ 4); no penalty amounts stated in this text (rule 4: no penaltyMax coded)

Not exclusively AI-specific: 'coordinating function' covers 'analyzing or processing nonpublic information through use of a system, software, algorithm, or other automated process' (§ 2) — algorithmic and non-algorithmic coordination alike

Relaxed pleading standard for civil actions: complaint 'need not allege facts tending to exclude the possibility of independent action' (§ 5.a(2)), limited to violations of § 3 of this act only (§ 5.b)

Carve-outs: licensed real estate brokers/broker-salespersons/salespersons (§§ 2, 3.a), aggregated-data reports and research/statistics/testing/training uses (§ 2), government entities under rental price restriction programs (§ 2), single-owner multi-property actions (§ 2), multiple listing services and their members (§ 7), third-party property managers acting in accordance with a rental contract (§ 8)

Non-company provisions noted per category rule: public education program by Dept. of Law and Public Safety and Dept. of Community Affairs (§ 9); AG + Commissioner of Community Affairs rulemaking (§ 10); municipal ordinances superseding the act prohibited (§ 6.b)
Effective 'on the first day of the fourth month next following the date of enactment' (§ 11)
